audit.why: Rumble is favoured early (Flamespitter out-ranges Warwick's 365-range Jaws of the Beast) and loses extended trades once Eternal Hunger's sub-50% healing turns on. The existing early/mid/late split already says exactly this, and the 47.41% over 715 games matches a lane Rumble wins on paper but loses to sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 1 spike text describes Warwick's sustain as 'passive healing on low-HP targets' without the actual threshold, so a player cannot act on it. Warwick's Eternal Hunger heals only below 50% HP and triples below 25%.
audit.why: Riot's own description for Eternal Hunger: heals below 50% health, triples below 25%. That is a hard number the player can play around — chip from full, and stop chipping once he is low.
audit.corrected: State the 50%/25% thresholds so the player knows poke is worth most before he is low, not after.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup, and it is the single ability that breaks Rumble's core pattern: 2.5s of damage reduction followed by a 1-second flee. The flee physically walks Rumble out of his own Flamespitter cone mid-channel. Blood Hunt (W) is also described only as 'a movement speed tool that closes small gaps' with no mention that it is conditional on the target being under 50% HP.
audit.why: Flamespitter is a 3-second cone that requires the target to stay in front of Rumble. A 1-second flee applied to Rumble ends the useful part of the cast, and the 2.5s damage reduction that precedes it eats the Danger Zone burst. Blood Hunt has no effect at all while Rumble is above 50% HP, which is precisely the argument for trading from full.
audit.corrected: Name Primal Howl, give its 15s rank-1 cooldown and the 2.5s / 1s structure, and tell the player to start Flamespitter after the howl resolves. Tie Blood Hunt to the 50%/25% thresholds. Add Grievous Wounds as the item answer to Jaws of the Beast plus Eternal Hunger.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown breakdown names Infinite Duress as 'matchup-defining' but gives no number, and omits Primal Howl entirely.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70s. At rank 1 that is nearly two minutes of free lane after he burns it — an actionable window, unlike 'track it'.
audit.corrected: Put the real numbers in: Infinite Duress 110/90/70, Primal Howl 15s at rank 1, The Equalizer 130s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game section claims Warwick wins 1v1s because 'the true damage and healing stack'. Warwick has no true damage anywhere in his kit, and anti-heal is never mentioned in the content layer despite being the deciding item in this lane.
audit.why: Riot's descriptions for Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress all list healing; none list true damage. Jaws of the Beast additionally deals max-health damage and heals for it, so Grievous Wounds is the correct answer.
audit.corrected: Delete the true-damage claim and replace it with the Grievous Wounds timing that actually decides extended fights.

edits.before: Warwick's passive healing on low-HP targets means early chip damage compounds against you — he sustains back Flamespitter poke faster than you expect.
edits.after: Eternal Hunger only heals him below 50% HP and triples under 25% — poke him from full, because every point of Flamespitter chip after that gets paid straight back.

edits.before: Reach 40% HP threshold to activate his passive movement speed and chase you down if your W shield is already spent
edits.after: Drop you under 50% so Blood Hunt speeds him straight at you — under 25% it triples and outruns your 6s Scrap Shield

edits.before: With W available he has a movement speed tool that closes small gaps; the lane is close but Rumble's double Electro-Harpoon slow can create genuine trade opportunities if he manages Heat precisely.
edits.after: Blood Hunt does nothing until you are under 50% HP, so trade from full: while you are healthy he walks in at base speed and your double Electro-Harpoon slow simply keeps him out of his 365-range Jaws of the Beast.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are where this lane turns against you: Warwick's sustained fighting with Q heal, passive sustain, and the threat of Infinite Duress suppress means extended trades increasingly favour him as HP drops on both sides. Your job is to win the first five seconds of every trade and hard stop — never let it become a drain fight. At Level 6, The Equalizer gives you a tool he cannot answer directly: drop it on his repositioning path after a trade to zone him off his healing window or punish a chase. The suppress threat of Infinite Duress means you should never stand within his jump range with your W shield on cooldown — always track it before committing your pattern.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 turn against you: Jaws of the Beast bites for max health and heals him for it, and once he is under 50% Eternal Hunger tops him back up, so any drain fight is his. Win the first five seconds and hard stop. Primal Howl is the trade-breaker nobody plans for — 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then a 1-second flee that walks you out of your own Flamespitter cone, so start Q after the howl resolves, not into it. At Level 6 Infinite Duress is 110 seconds at rank 1: the moment he spends it you own almost two minutes of lane, and The Equalizer on his retreat path punishes a chase he has no way to cancel.

edits.before: In the late game Warwick's itemisation (Black Cleaver, Divine Sunderer) makes him far more dangerous than his lane appearance suggests — he can now run through your W shield in a sustained fight and the true damage and healing stack means he wins most 1v1s if he connects Infinite Duress. Your role flips entirely to your Equalizer: it remains one of the strongest teamfight ultimates in the game and you do not need to win this 1v1 to win the game. Drop The Equalizer across choke points, baron pit, and dragon circles and let the AoE slow plus magic damage do the work while your team follows. Avoid isolating yourself near Warwick when his Infinite Duress is off cooldown — the suppress chains directly into a kill if your W is spent.
edits.after: In the late game Warwick's itemisation (Black Cleaver, Divine Sunderer) makes him far more dangerous than his lane appearance suggests — he runs through your W shield in a sustained fight and his stacked healing wins most 1v1s once Infinite Duress connects, so Grievous Wounds is not optional: pick up Oblivion Orb before your second full item. Your role flips to your Equalizer, still one of the strongest teamfight ultimates in the game, and you do not need this 1v1 to win the game. Drop it across choke points, the baron pit and dragon circles and let the slow plus magic damage work while your team follows. Never isolate yourself near Warwick with Infinite Duress up — the suppress chains straight into a kill if your W is spent.

notes: Two packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Use The Equalizer' (wants.you[2]) and 'Land Infinite Duress' (wants.foe[2]) are both the correct Riot names — left untouched. Rumble's kit file flags Scrap Shield (W) with 'knockup' and 'terrain'; Riot's own description is only a shield plus a burst of move speed, so those two derived flags are tooltip-parsing misfires. I did not write any Scrap-Shield-blocks-dashes advice, and the _missing-interactions entry 'Your Scrap Shield (W), The Equalizer (R) shuts off Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q), Infinite Duress (R)' rests on that bad flag — Scrap Shield does not stop either. The Equalizer only slows; it does not physically block his leap. Item names 'Divine Sunderer' and 'Black Cleaver' were already in the text and I could not verify them against the 26.15 item pool, so I left them as written.
